# review-export — Review export — commit-pinned JSON snapshot of a release

# Review export — `rivet review export`

```
rivet review export --release <version> [--since <ref>] [--format json]
```

Hands a release to an external reviewer as one JSON document that is
pinned to a commit. The reviewer can check out `commit` and see exactly
what was exported; a later `--since <that commit>` export shows only what
changed for the release since that review.

## What is exported

Every artifact **scoped to the release** — the same set as
`rivet list --release <version>`: artifacts whose `release:` field equals
`<version>`. Artifacts are sorted by id.

## Clean tree required

The export refuses to run on a dirty working tree, because it would not
match the commit it names. "Dirty" is any entry of
`git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` — **untracked files count**,
because an untracked YAML file under an artifact source is loaded by rivet
and would land in a snapshot that claims to be `HEAD`. Ignored files do not
count. The command exits non-zero, prints nothing on stdout, and names each
dirty path on stderr. It also fails outside a git repository or before the
first commit.

## JSON shape

```json
{
  "command": "review-export",
  "commit": "<full 40-character sha of HEAD>",
  "release": "v0.42.0",
  "since": null,
  "count": 1,
  "artifacts": [
    {
      "id": "REQ-001",
      "type": "requirement",
      "title": "Text-file-first artifact management",
      "status": "approved",
      "release": "v0.42.0",
      "description": "Multi-line description, or null",
      "tags": ["core"],
      "fields": { "priority": "must" },
      "fields_per_variant": {},
      "links": [ { "type": "satisfies", "target": "SC-1" } ],
      "provenance": {
        "created-by": "ai-assisted",
        "model": "claude-opus-4-6",
        "timestamp": "2026-03-01T12:00:00Z"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Every key is always present. An unset `status`, `release`, `description`
or `provenance` is `null`, never omitted and never a placeholder like `-`.
`provenance` keys are the YAML spellings (`created-by`, `model`,
`session-id`, `timestamp`, `reviewed-by`, `federation`), each present only
when set.

## `--since <ref>`: what changed for this release

With `--since`, the project is also loaded as it was at `<ref>` (the
tracked tree, through `git archive`, the same loader as
`rivet impact --since`), and `since` holds the full sha `<ref>` resolved
to. `artifacts` then holds only the artifacts whose export differs, each
with one extra key:

| `change`  | Meaning | Content |
|-----------|---------|---------|
| `added`   | In the release at HEAD, not at `<ref>` | as at HEAD |
| `removed` | In the release at `<ref>`, not at HEAD | as at `<ref>` |
| `changed` | In the release at both, export differs | as at HEAD |

A `changed` artifact also carries `changed_fields`: the artifact keys whose
values differ, in the order above, e.g. `["status", "description", "links"]`.
A change inside a custom field is reported as `fields`.

Scope is per release: an artifact that **moved into** the release (its
`release:` changed to `<version>`) is `added`, and one that **moved out**
or was deleted is `removed`. Artifacts that did not change are absent.

## Formats and exit codes

`json` is the only format (and the default). Exit 0 on success; non-zero
on a dirty tree, an unresolvable `--since` ref, or a non-git project.

## Contract

`schemas/json/review-export-output.schema.json` (also listed by
`rivet schema list-json`) is the machine-readable contract; a contract test
validates real output against it.
